questions.question: Define conservation and sustainable use. Give three ecosystem services and explain why South Africa is important for world biodiversity.
questions.expected_answer: Conservation is the protection, careful management and wise use of natural resources and ecosystems so that they continue to function and remain available for future generations. Sustainable use means using a resource no faster than it can be replaced, so it lasts indefinitely. Ecosystem services: catchments supplying water, wetlands filtering water and absorbing floods, pollination of crops by insects, birds and bats, soil fertility from soil organisms, fish from the sea, tourism, medicinal plants. South Africa covers about 2% of the world's land but has close to 10% of its plant species; the Cape Floral Region has about 9 000 plant species, roughly 70% endemic, so species lost here are lost everywhere.

questions.question: Describe four methods used by environmentalists and organisations to conserve ecosystems, with a South African example of each.
questions.expected_answer: Any four: protected areas, e.g. Kruger National Park (Sabie Game Reserve 1898, national park 1926) or Marine Protected Areas (20 new in 2019), where breeding stocks spill over into fished areas; laws and regulation, e.g. the Biodiversity Act of 2004, fishing quotas and closed seasons, permits for cycads, CITES banning trade in rhino horn and ivory; rescue and direct protection, e.g. anti-poaching rangers and dehorning of rhino, SANCCOB cleaning about 19 000 oiled penguins after the Treasure spill of 2000, captive breeding and seed banks; restoration, e.g. Working for Water clearing alien trees since 1995, dune rehabilitation; research, monitoring and education, e.g. SANBI Red Lists, Endangered Wildlife Trust, BirdLife South Africa.

questions.question: Give four actions an individual can take to conserve ecosystems, linking each to the disruption it reduces, and use the five steps to evaluate a plan to close fishing near African penguin colonies.
questions.expected_answer: Actions, e.g.: saving water leaves more water in rivers and wetlands; saving electricity reduces coal burning, air pollution and climate change; reducing, reusing and recycling keeps waste out of landfills, rivers and the sea; buying only SASSI green seafood and never poached perlemoen or rhino products reduces overharvesting; planting indigenous and removing aliens reduces alien invasion and supports pollinators; staying on paths protects nests. Plan: problem is penguin decline, main cause shortage of sardines and anchovy from overfishing; the plan closes purse-seine fishing near colonies; it targets the cause, so it is strong; the fishing industry bears a cost and penguins and tourism benefit; success measured by counting breeding pairs over several years.
